summary: A Geant4 study record could be re-issued validated-in-scope on evidence that does not support it: a benchmark grade declared by the record, a scope that did not compare the observable or left dimensions undeclared, a target that was not isolated, a convergence gate without an equivalence test or with the finest scan value missing, and negative controls compared across units in one direction.

database_specific.introduced_basis: contracts 3.1.0 (Geant4 phase 2) made a study record re-issued validated-in-scope possible; it was first released in 0.20.0, and the affected scripts existed before without any record able to carry the label

observables: the validated-in-scope label of Geant4 study records and its scope
the convergence gate verdict and the detection limits of their benchmarks
whether an F4 design evaluation counts (contracts/design.py takes only validated-in-scope studies)
impact.bias: the gate passed about 50 % of the time at a true change equal to the tolerance (now 0.05); a study that passed an MPV benchmark could label any observable or undeclared range validated-in-scope; a missing finest scan point let the gate pass on coarser ones
impact.trigger: validated-in-scope study records whose scope, benchmarks or scan differ from what their evidence covers; J14's own decisions are unchanged

applies_to.match_basis: a Geant4 study record carries extension.study and, from contracts 3.5.0, the check_geant4_study.py trace (a study record without validated-in-scope is listed too: its label was not upgraded, but its benchmarks and gate may still be affected); an F4 design-evaluation is built on such a record. A simulated dataset-record shows no field that tells whether its input study was affected: check its input study record instead

remedy: regenerate the study records with this version (check_geant4_study.py run and label --upgrade on run summaries from adapters/geant4/assets/summary_from_csv.py); after a study is re-issued, redo its F4 evaluations with evaluate_design.py f4 --replace (the old ones become stale once the study's hash changes); rerun contracts/dependencies.py on simulated dataset-records that use the study
